# nanovna-saver

**Desktop companion for the NanoVNA — bigger screen, real calibration, exportable data**

- **Version recorded:** 0.7.3
- **Categories:** `antenna`, `electronics`, `hardware`
- **Upstream:** <https://github.com/NanoVNA-Saver/nanovna-saver>

## What it does

Drives a NanoVNA over USB from a PC: runs sweeps wider and with more points than the device's own screen allows, performs and stores calibrations, displays Smith charts, SWR, return loss and impedance, averages multiple sweeps, and exports Touchstone s1p and s2p files for other tools.

## Why you would want it

The NanoVNA is a remarkable instrument attached to a postage-stamp display and four buttons. Everything that makes a VNA useful -- seeing the whole sweep, calibrating properly, keeping the measurement -- is painful on the device and straightforward here. Touchstone export is the part that matters most: a measurement you cannot get out of the instrument is a measurement you cannot compare.

## Before it will work

A NanoVNA on USB, and permission to open its serial port -- membership of the `dialout` group, which the hardware catalog requests and which does not apply to a session already open. A calibration kit, or the loads that came with the device; an uncalibrated sweep is a picture, not a measurement.

## How it installs

- apt: `nanovna-saver`

## Known problems

The NanoVNA family is a large set of clones with different firmware and different serial protocols, and support varies -- a device that enumerates is not necessarily one this speaks to correctly. AHRL installs it into a per-user venv from an unpinned git clone (inventory unit 85); this uses the packaged version instead, which is older and does not move under you. Calibration is stored per-session unless saved, and the commonest mistake is a sweep taken outside the calibrated range, which produces confident nonsense at the edges.
